summary.intent: Investigate what happens when a jobSpec references a cuebot layer limit that doesn't exist, then implement improved error handling so job launch still fails closed but returns a clear exception naming the missing limits.
summary.outcome: Delivered a working fix on branch joblaunch_missing_limits: a new LimitDao.findMissingLimitNames query, synchronous pre-launch validation in JobLauncher that throws a descriptive EntityCreationError listing missing limits and their job/layer references, defense-in-depth validation in JobManagerService.addLayerLimits, new tests (JobLauncherLimitTests, LimitDaoTests.testFindMissingLimitNames) all passing, spotless applied, and changes committed.

repo: Layer limit names in a JobSpec are never validated at parse time (JobSpec.java and pyoutline cue.py just collect/serialize the strings) — validation only happened at DB insert time before this change.

JobManagerService.createJob previously resolved limit names via LimitDao.findLimit per layer, which throws Spring's EmptyResultDataAccessException (an unhelpful raw exception) if the name doesn't exist.
createJob/launchJobSpec run under @Transactional(REQUIRED), so any exception mid-launch rolls back the entire spec (all jobs/layers/frames), not just the offending layer.

JobLauncher.launch swallows exceptions from the launch queue thread and calls emailSupport.reportLaunchError instead of surfacing them to the RPC caller — this is why launchSpec (async) previously returned success even though the job silently failed to launch.

launchSpecAndWait surfaces failures via whiteboard.findJob on a job that was never committed, producing a misleading gRPC INTERNAL 'Incorrect result size: expected 1, actual 0' error unrelated to the real cause.
AdminManager/AdminManagerService already had a jobLauncher property wired in applicationContext-service.xml, so no new Spring bean wiring was needed to expose limit lookups to JobLauncher.

pycue only maps a fixed set of gRPC status codes (NOT_FOUND/ALREADY_EXISTS/DEADLINE/INTERNAL/UNAVAILABLE/CANCELLED) to specific exceptions; anything else (e.g. INVALID_ARGUMENT) falls through to a generic CueException, and ManageJob catches generic Exception for all launch failures.

code.finding: createJob previously called limitDao.findLimit(name).getLimitId() per layer limit with no existence check, causing EmptyResultDataAccessException on undefined limits.
Added findMissingLimitNames(Collection<String>) to batch-check limit existence via a single WHERE str_name IN (...) query, returning missing names deduped in input order.
Added verifyLimits, invoked from verifyJobSpec, which runs synchronously for both queueAndLaunch and launch, so it now rejects the RPC before queueing instead of failing asynchronously.
Added addLayerLimits as a defense-in-depth check for limits that vanish between spec verification and DB insert, throwing a descriptive JobLaunchException instead of a raw DAO exception.

workflow: Traced a bug end-to-end (parsing → service → DAO → transaction → RPC servant → client mapping) before writing any code, which shaped a fix that addressed both the async and sync launch paths.
Ran spotlessApply before final diff review to keep formatting consistent with project style.
Verified the fix with targeted test runs (JobManagerTests, JobSpecTests, AdminManagerTests, WhiteboardDaoTests) rather than the full suite, plus new purpose-built tests.

friction: The existing failure mode was actively misleading: the async launchSpec RPC returned success while the job silently failed later, and launchSpecAndWait returned an unrelated 'Incorrect result size' gRPC error, both obscuring the true cause (missing limit).
open_items: gRPC status for this failure was deliberately left as INTERNAL rather than INVALID_ARGUMENT to avoid breaking pycue's existing exception mapping and changing behavior for other existing errors (show-missing/job-pending); user can request this cleanup as a follow-up.
